newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures settled higher after a relatively calm session, helped by Bund strength and a continuation of the favourable bond market sentiment following the reaction to Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report.
The September bond future climbed early in the session then remained stuck in a narrow range near the day's highs for the rest of the session and traders said the market remained bullish.
PIBOR contracts benefitted from the stability of the franc and one trader said there were some short positions hanging over from last week which remain to be squeezed out.
The franc clung onto most of Friday's gains throughout the day and was then driven to a high of 3.4129 per mark at 1520 GMT as the dollar climbed against the German unit.

Nick Parsons, foreign exchange strategist at Banque Paribas said "forecasts of a franc crisis are in the process of being reappraised, there are doubts creeping in and it looks like we're going to get through till the end of September."

He said the belief that agreement was near on a budget discipline pact for countries in a single currency reinforced the view that Germany would be more likely to support France in defending its currency against speculative attack.
He also said the lack of a coordinated union response so far to planned government cutbacks was helping the currency.
Ciaran O'Hagan, bond analyst at JP Morgan in Paris said, however, the outcome of a meeting on Tuesday between several French unions would need to be watched closely.
He said lingering concern about potential union unrest may have been holding back two-year government bonds on Monday.
Traders said much of the activity in bond futures trading on Monday centred on rolling over positions from the September conctract, which expires on September 16, into the December contract.
One trader said he expected the September contract to remain stuck in a range between 123.34 and 123.90 for the next two sessions.
Another said the contract could well test its previous contract high at 124.10 but there would need to be an increase in volume for any sustainable attack.
As expected the African Development Bank issued two billion francs of bonds. It sold a 6.50 percent 2006 bond priced at 17 basis points over OATs.
